title: The Semester of Maple Street
premise: Lior Lockridge has spent twelve years perfecting the art of being overlooked, ever since a childhood accident she can barely remember fractured her family and sent them to Maple Street to start over. When her history teacher pairs her with Marisol Vega—the girl who tormented her all of middle school—for a semester project excavating the school's buried past, Lior discovers the school was built over a demolished neighborhood whose residents were erased, including, impossibly, someone connected to her own forgotten memory. As the project forces Lior and Marisol into uneasy alliance, Lior must choose between protecting her best friend Theo's version of events and telling the truth about what really happened the night everything changed. In the end, Lior testifies at the school board hearing and performs the truth in front of the whole school at the spring audition, losing Theo's friendship but gaining a self she no longer has to hide.
about_author: T. M. Kavanagh is a former substitute teacher who spent three years collecting rumors about the old buildings in her Rust Belt hometown before any of them became stories. The Semester of Maple Street is her second novel for young adults.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Overlooked
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On her first day at Halloway High, Lior demonstrates her twelve-year mastery of invisibility—sitting at edges, answering only when called. But a class roster error seats her next to Marisol Vega, who recognizes her from middle school and says so out loud. Beat: dread that her careful walls have already cracked.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mr. Okafor announces the semester-long local history project and pairs nemesis with nemesis: Lior and Marisol will document 'what stood before Halloway.' Theo promises Lior he'll help her survive it. Beat: trapped fury, and a flicker of curiosity she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Basement Permissions
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol, surprisingly competent and bossy, gets them access to the school basement archives. She treats Lior like a partner, not a target, which unsettles Lior more than cruelty would. They find a 1960s plat map of a vanished street. Beat: grudging respect disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Maple Street
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The vanished street was called Maple Street—the same name as Lior's own address. Her mother goes quiet when asked, changing the subject with practiced ease. That night Lior finds a box of photos she's never been allowed to open. Beat: the first real crack in her family's careful silence.

chapters.title: Theo Knows Best
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo warns Lior to drop the Maple Street angle, oddly insistent, and offers to do her bibliography as a bribe. His loyalty feels heavier than usual. Beat: love that controls, and Lior noticing it for the first time.

chapters.title: The Demolition File
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The pair uncovers news clippings: in 1971 the district razed sixteen homes on Maple Street, displacing families who were promised relocation that never fully came. One displaced family's surname matches Lior's mother's maiden name. Beat: Marisol watches Lior connect the dots and chooses not to gloat.

chapters.title: Truce Over Fries
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Working late at a diner, Lior and Marisol accidentally trade real things—Marisol's father's deportation fear, Lior's fogged memory of an accident at age four. Neither calls it friendship. Beat: two guarded people discovering the other is also guarding something.

chapters.title: What Theo Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback chapter: Theo was there the day of Lior's accident, and his account—which everyone accepted—is not what happened. He's spent twelve years being the loyal witness. Beat: guilt calcifying into protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Audition Notice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Spring auditions are posted for the school's oral-history performance night; Mr. Okafor strongly suggests the project pairs present their findings on stage. Lior hasn't spoken publicly since elementary school. Marisol signs them up without asking. Beat: terror and, underneath it, want.

chapters.title: Interview with Mrs. Okonkwo
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They interview an elderly former Maple Street resident who remembers 'the Lockridge girl'—Lior's grandmother—and describes the night of the demolition fire. Details don't match the family story Lior was raised on. Beat: the past becoming a living argument.

chapters.title: Mother, Closed Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior confronts her mother with the clippings; her mother forbids the project topic, revealing only that the family paid a price for silence. Lior overhears her mother call Theo's mother, and the conversation sounds like a pact. Beat: betrayal reframing every kindness.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Their archive box disappears from the classroom; Marisol accuses Theo, Lior defends him, and the fragile alliance shatters. Lior chooses Theo by default—and hates how easy the choice was. Beat: loyalty winning over truth, and costing her.

chapters.title: Working Alone
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol rebuilds the research solo from county records, finding the fire report: the blaze started in the Lockridge house, and a child was carried out by a neighbor's son—a boy named Theo's father's name. Beat: Marisol deciding whether to use the truth as a weapon or a bridge.

chapters.title: The Box Under the Bed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior finally opens the forbidden photo box: images of Maple Street before the demolition, her grandmother's face, and a newspaper photo of the rescue with a boy who is unmistakably Theo's father. Her memory begins returning in fragments. Beat: grief and vertigo as the careful life reveals its foundations.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Creek
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lior asks Theo directly. He admits his father pulled her from the fire, that both families agreed on a story to bury the neighborhood's shame and their own entanglement, and that Theo has been enforcing it out of love. Beat: the friendship breaking honestly, without villains.

chapters.title: Reconciliation Terms
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior apologizes to Marisol—not for doubting her, but for choosing comfort over truth. Marisol sets terms: they finish this together, and Lior speaks on stage, in her own voice, about her own street. Beat: alliance rebuilt on harder ground.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Rehearsals for the performance night; Lior's voice shakes through every run-through while Theo watches from the back row, neither forgiven nor gone. Mr. Okafor tells Lior that memory isn't disloyalty. Beat: courage assembling itself line by line.

chapters.title: The Board Hearing
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A school board member moves to shut down the project after complaints from old families. Lior testifies publicly for the first time in twelve years, naming Maple Street and the sixteen houses. Beat: the invisible girl made visible, terrified and unstoppered.

chapters.title: What My Mother Never Said
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Her mother attends the hearing unannounced and, afterward, finally tells the whole story—including her own role in agreeing to silence. Not absolution, but a beginning. Beat: inherited secrets set down, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Audition Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. Before the packed auditorium, Lior and Marisol perform the history of Maple Street, ending with Lior telling her own story—the accident, the rescue, the years of carefulness. Theo, in the audience, stands and adds the piece only he can give. Beat: truth offered as a gift, not a weapon.

chapters.title: After the Applause
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Theo doesn't come back, and Lior lets the friendship rest rather than begging for the old shape of it. Marisol saves her a seat at lunch—permanently, it seems. Beat: mourning and belonging arriving together.

chapters.title: The New Street Name
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Lior's POV. Months later, the district votes to install a memorial plaque honoring Maple Street's families, and Lior's name is on the dedication. She walks home on Maple Street no longer careful, no longer invisible. Beat: quiet, earned belonging.
